newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa -Agreement with Lagardere is binding.
newsitem.headline: Dasa -Agreement with Lagardere is binding.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG said on Wednesday it expected to follow through with a defence and space partnership with Lagardere even if the French firm's bid for Thomson-CSF fails.
"The contents of our memorandum of understanding are binding," said Dasa spokesman Christian Poppe.
Dasa, in announcing the pact with Lagardere in May, said it would give its "total and unconditional support for Lagardere's bid to buy Thomson-CSF."

Paris has planned to sell its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF, a defence electronics group, but the Socialists who came to power in elections this month said during their campaign they would stop all privatisations.
Alcatel Alsthom was also bidding for Thomson-CSF.
Under their pact, Dasa and Lagardere agreed to let Matra BAe Dynamics, a joint venture between Lagardere and British Aerospace Plc, take a 30 percent stake in Dasa's LFK missile business.

Matra BAe could increase the stake to 49 percent within two and a half years, and would have a pre-emptive right to buy the unit if Dasa wanted to sell it to a non-domestic buyer, Lagardere executives said.
The partners also agreed to combine Dasa's space operations with Matra Marconi Space, a venture owned 51 percent by Lagardere and 49 percent by Britain's General Electric Co Plc.
